body:
## Thesis

In a consumer repository the gate prints a green `RESULT: PASS` while several of its passing checks scan an empty scope, and the product tree is not inside any of them. `SKIP` cannot fail by construction, so "not configured" and "nothing to check" are indistinguishable from "checked and clean". This is the same silent-green class as #48 and #51, reached by configuration scoping instead of shell-probe bugs.

## Measured in the consumer tree (verbatim outputs in `00-vacuous-green.txt`)

| Check as printed by `grok_verify --mode pr` | Independent measurement |
| --- | --- |
| `PASS bandit: exit=0` | `bandit -c bandit.yaml -r engineering` → `Total lines of code: 0`. Control on `scripts`: `Total lines of code: 833`. The probe flips, so the 0 is real. Cause: `bandit.yaml:exclude_dirs` names `engineering` |
| `PASS ruff: exit=0` | `ruff.toml: exclude = [..., "engineering", ...]` — the same tree is out of scope |
| `PASS contract-structure: 0 contracts checked` | nothing was checked |
| `PASS sql-safety: 0 unsafe SQL findings` | no SQL in tree; passes on emptiness |
| `SKIP architecture` / `SKIP governance` / `SKIP workflow-artifacts` | `verification.py:1060` — `overall = "fail" if counts["fail"] else "pass"`: a SKIP can never lower the verdict |
| (absence of any product check) | `grep -c '\.swift\|xcodeproj\|\.tmx' verification.py` → **0**; the token `swift` appears exactly once in `.grok-stack/adaptive_grok/*.py`, in `architecture.py:720`, a config-gated path that is `SKIP` in every consumer run I have seen |

Product surface left at 0 % by the gate in this tree: 18 Swift files / 4 227 LOC, 125 `.tmx`, 153 `.png`, `.xcodeproj`. Of the 10 passing checks, 4 inspect the installed stack (`factory-*`), 5 pass on empty scope or whitespace, 1 is a self-check of the fingerprint.

## Why this is not just "configure it"

The stack installs `bandit.yaml`, `ruff.toml` and `.coveragerc` into the consumer tree with the **factory's own** exclusions (`engineering` is a directory the factory creates for its own records). Upstream #110 already covers "refresh silently overwrites `.coveragerc` / `bandit.yaml` / `routing.json`"; this report is about the other half — the installed defaults are scoped to a tree that is not the consumer's product, and nothing in the run tells the operator that the green verdict is silent about the product.

## Direction (not a demand)

1. A check that reports a scope count must fail (or at least `warn`) when the count is 0 while changed files of that language exist in the diff — "0 lines scanned" next to 55 changed files is not a pass.
2. `overall` should degrade to `incomplete` (distinct from `pass`) while any configured-but-inapplicable check is `SKIP`, and the receipt should carry the skipped list.
3. Installer should emit language-appropriate scope files per consumer (or leave them out and let the gate report "not configured" instead of passing on emptiness).

## Evidence files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `00-vacuous-green.txt` | gate output lines for the run, plus my bandit A/B (0 vs 833 LOC), `ruff.toml`, `bandit.yaml`, `verification.py:1060`, the `.swift/.tmx/.xcodeproj` grep count |

---

Evidence bundle (secret gist): <https://gist.github.com/Dimkox/de7b79a4fb3a6590216c3245838fbe06>
title: Gate prints PASS from checks whose installed config scans nothing (0 LOC bandit/ruff exclude engineering; no product-language check at all)
